content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Database-backed tests should use temporary service instances, wait for readiness, use test-only credentials, apply migrations, and clean up after the job. A useful CI pipeline gives a clear pass/fail result for relevant quality checks. Keep fast checks early, use services only when tests need them, and ensure required checks cannot be skipped accidentally. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.title: Starting database services
items.text: Use a temporary service with explicit port, test credentials, and readiness checks for CI. Production migrations need backward-compatibility, backup/recovery, and deployment-order planning.

items.title: Temporary credentials
items.text: Store credentials in the appropriate protected secret store, pass them only to the step that needs them, and never print or save them in logs, summaries, artifacts, or caches.

items.title: Database readiness checks
items.text: Use a temporary service with explicit port, test credentials, and readiness checks for CI. Production migrations need backward-compatibility, backup/recovery, and deployment-order planning.

items.title: Schema migration tests
items.text: Use a temporary service with explicit port, test credentials, and readiness checks for CI. Production migrations need backward-compatibility, backup/recovery, and deployment-order planning.

items.title: Cleanup after test execution
items.text: Make the check deterministic and fail with a meaningful status when requirements are not met. Preserve reports where useful and configure required branch checks to match the checks the workflow actually emits.

content_blocks.code:
jobs:
  integration:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: test
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test-only
          POSTGRES_DB: app_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U test -d app_test"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - run: echo "Run integration tests after service readiness"
content_blocks.expected_output: The job starts an isolated PostgreSQL service with a health check; a real test command must wait for readiness and use the service credentials only for disposable data.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use on a test workflow. Do not reuse production credentials or connect untrusted contributions to a production database.

content.expected_output: The expected result is the behavior described here: Database-backed tests should use temporary service instances, wait for readiness, use test-only credentials, apply migrations, and clean up after the job. The real result depends on the repository, selected ref, configured permissions, and runner availability.
troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
